items.title: Somalia: Six Million Somalis Face Acute Hunger As Drought and Conflict Worsen
items.description: [RFI] Six million people in Somalia are facing acute hunger, with nearly two million children at emergency levels, as severe drought, conflict and falling humanitarian funding deepen what the UN describes as one of the world's worst malnutrition crises. Medical charity MSF tells RFI it's sounding the alarm "before it's too late".
items.titleIt: Somalia: Six Million Somalis Face Acute Hunger As Drought and Conflict Worsen

items.title: Somalia: Mogadishu's 'Forced' Eviction Turns Into War
items.description: [Radio Dalsan] The demolition of homes in Tookiyo neighbourhood, in Mogadishu's Yaqshiid district, has triggered tensions and clashes between government forces and local residents who opposed the operation. The demolitions began around midnight and were still continuing, with local reports saying nearly 10 people had been injured in the confrontation.
items.titleIt: Somalia: Mogadishu's 'Forced' Eviction Turns Into War

items.title: Somalia: Somalia Says It Is Aware of Military Operations Off Puntland Coast

items.title: Journalist Mascuud Warsame tells SJS about his 39-day ordeal in Somalia's spy agency detention facility
items.description: On 30 June 2026, Mascuud Warsame, journalist and founder of an online media platform, Xogbile, was kidnapped by three armed NISA officers shortly after leaving his workplace on Maka Al-Mukarama Avenue in Somalia's capital, Mogadishu. items.title: Somalia's New Speaker Got His Parliamentary Seat Through a Military Operation. His Career Was Built by Turkey.
items.description: That minister was Abdulkadir Mohamed Nur Jaamac — known in Somali political circles as Madaxa Na Furan. On 11 August 2026, he was confirmed as Speaker of Somalia's House of the People, winning 142 votes against his opponent's 30 in a vote that lawmakers from Puntland and Jubaland boycotted as illegitimate. The story of how he arrived at the Speaker's chair — and what it means for the parliament he now leads — has not yet been told in full. items.titleIt: Somalia's New Speaker Got His Parliamentary Seat Through a Military Operation. His Career Was Built by Turkey.

items.title: Somali Cabinet Approves Passport, Trade and Judicial Reforms
items.description: The council was briefed on Somalia's new third-generation electronic passport and was told that changes to personal data in issued passports have been stopped entirely to strengthen the document's credibility. Ministers also approved a Rules of Origin Bill allowing goods containing at least 30% Somali content to qualify for preferential treatment in regional markets. The law is aimed at boosting local production and exports following Somalia's entry into the East African Community and its participation in the African Continental Free Trade Area. items.titleIt: Somali Cabinet Approves Passport, Trade and Judicial Reforms

items.title: New Chapter, Same Stalemate: Somalia’s War with Al-Shabaab
items.description: The Somali government’s battle with Al-Shabaab militants grinds on, with neither able to gain a decisive advantage. items.titleIt: Merz spokesman says sees no conflict between Berlin and Rome on migrants
